rubrics.intent_basis: Expansion log R1-R3: node isolation was dispersed through mutation and traversal callers.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Generic tree mutation, mutable lookup, scan, and ordinal paths each decide node generation and publish a copied root or child locally.
rubrics.criterion: Centralize the generic tree's copy-on-write eligibility and slot publication across mutation, mutable reads, scans, and ordinal operations while retaining their distinct traversal results.
rubrics.acceptance: A shared boundary determines whether each visited node needs isolation and publishes it to the actual root or child slot across those paths. Existing owner methods, shared policy data, or complete-operation reconnection qualify; do not require an extra abstraction or exact historical helper. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Extracting only nodeSet's repeated block while getHint, nodeScan, and getAt retain independent generation decisions.

rubrics.intent_basis: Expansion log R1-R3: map isolation was independently spread over its operation families.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Map mutation, mutable traversal, extrema, rank, and iterator code repeat generation checks and slot replacement.
rubrics.criterion: Give map node isolation a shared decision and publication boundary used across its mutation, mutable traversal, extrema, rank, and iterator paths.
rubrics.acceptance: The affected map callers use one coherent rule for isolating a shared node at its root or child location; read-only access remains read-only. Existing owner methods, shared policy data, or complete-operation reconnection qualify; do not require an extra abstraction or exact historical helper. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Consolidating map Set and Delete while mutable scans, getAt, and MapIter still embed the same policy.

rubrics.intent_basis: Deepening batch 2 split node allocation from copy callbacks, child storage, and publication.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Both copy methods allocate metadata and item arrays only; individual callers choose Copy versus IsoCopy, duplicate child arrays, and publish the isolated node.
rubrics.criterion: Make optional payload-copy precedence and invocation a coherent policy across node isolation consumers.
rubrics.acceptance: Copy takes precedence over IsoCopy; generic items and Map values invoke their applicable hooks in stored order only on eligible isolation. Map keys remain unchanged. Metadata/item allocation alone is not complete isolation; child topology preparation is assessed independently below. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Moving only the item callback loop to a helper while callers still independently determine precedence or child copying.

rubrics.intent_basis: Expansion log R1 identified duplicate default and minimum degree normalization.
rubrics.baseline_defect: BTreeG.init and Map.init each implement the same degree default, degree-one promotion, and min/max arithmetic.
rubrics.criterion: Make changes to the currently supported default, degree-one, and explicit-degree occupancy rules possible at one boundary used by both tree implementations.
rubrics.acceptance: Default, degree-one, and ordinary degree bounds have one maintainable rule used by both initializers; changing the default or minimum rule does not require parallel edits. Existing owner methods, shared policy data, or complete-operation reconnection qualify; do not require an extra abstraction or exact historical helper. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Adding a wrapper around either initializer while leaving two independent arithmetic branches.

rubrics.intent_basis: Expansion scattered split accounting; deepening batch 1 coupled right aggregation, left subtraction, and root publication.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Generic and map splits calculate right counts locally, then parent and root callers separately derive left counts from an incoming total and separator contribution.
rubrics.criterion: Give subtree-count conservation during node split a coherent owner across right, left, separator, and new-root publication for both implementations.
rubrics.acceptance: A split's count update is governed by one consistent conservation rule, including the one separator item and unchanged total container count. Existing owner methods, shared policy data, or complete-operation reconnection qualify; do not require an extra abstraction or exact historical helper. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Centralizing right-child aggregation only while parent/root callers still perform unrelated left-count subtraction.

rubrics.intent_basis: Both generic and map implementations maintain subtree totals used by rank and deletion paths.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Delete callers in both files compute a sibling-pair total and repair a child's count after nodeRebalance, while the rebalance branches separately alter right counts during merge or rotation.
rubrics.criterion: Coordinate deletion's sibling-count handoff with merge and rotation count updates in btreeg.go and map.go, independently of insertion split accounting.
rubrics.acceptance: Each file has one consistent rebalance-count contract for merge and both rotation directions, so delete callers do not duplicate branch-specific arithmetic. Existing owner methods, shared policy data, or complete-operation reconnection qualify; do not require an extra abstraction or exact historical helper. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Consolidating insertion split counts while delete and nodeRebalance still divide sibling-count arithmetic between caller and callee.

rubrics.intent_basis: Deepening batch2 and retry traversal lifecycle split.
rubrics.baseline_defect: nodeScan/nodeReverse/nodeWalk/nodeItems publish payload-only clones and branch using original topology before completing child-vector isolation.
rubrics.criterion: Give mutable traversal a coherent complete-isolation contract before descending or delivering callbacks.
rubrics.acceptance: Original topology, replacement identity and child-array preparation must agree: copied internal nodes are not mistaken for leaves, original snapshot child slices remain isolated, and leaf paths never dereference missing children. Read-only and already-owned nodes avoid optional copy hooks. A complete loader or redesigned traversal may satisfy both this item and payload policy SS03. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Consolidating only entry eligibility while leaving independent topology/preparation decisions in each traversal is insufficient.
